research_basis.authoring_method: Original synthesis using the user brief and the THE DMI implementation reference as the structural benchmark.
research_basis.licence_handling: Original implementation content informed by Jisc structure. Jisc digital maturity materials are published under terms including CC BY-NC-SA on the main toolkit page; scenarios and practitioner language here are independently written.
notes: The source brief describes a 3-level model and requests 10 boundaries. This implementation therefore operationalises the two assessable adjacent boundaries in a 3-level model: Established to Enhanced (EM) and Enhanced to Mature (MM).
The brief also mentioned EE as a target-level code; that label is retained in metadata as an entry-threshold alias rather than a scored boundary.

mappings.target_construct: People & Culture across all pillars; Strategy as enabling dependency
what_transfers: shared norms, confidence, change readiness, and cultural adoption
mappings.rationale: Both frameworks treat culture and people as an essential enabler of mature digital transformation.

mappings.target_construct: Technology + Utilisation intersections across Teaching, Research, Professional Services, and Planning/Governance
what_transfers: innovation through digital experimentation, scaling, and adoption
what_does_not_transfer: THE separates innovation effects by pillar rather than holding one cross-institution innovation dimension
mappings.rationale: Jisc innovation is broader and more synthetic; THE distributes related issues across child dimensions.

what_transfers: digital capability building, workforce readiness, and confidence
what_does_not_transfer: THE captures people capability at pillar level rather than as a single development dimension
mappings.rationale: The strongest conceptual overlap is in capability and culture.

mappings.target_construct: Data + Utilisation across all pillars; Strategy dependency
what_transfers: knowledge sharing, evidence use, and decision support
what_does_not_transfer: THE separates knowledge use into data and utilisation rather than one management dimension
mappings.rationale: Both frameworks care about whether information flows into better decisions and practice.

mappings.target_construct: Planning & Governance and Professional Services child dimensions with external-facing utilisation
what_does_not_transfer: THE DMI has no single standalone partnership dimension
mappings.rationale: THE captures some partnership effects indirectly, but Jisc exchange is more explicit.

what_transfers: leadership signals, readiness, and shared culture for change
what_does_not_transfer: AI-specific governance, literacy, and responsible-use content in the AI framework
mappings.rationale: Digital culture provides the substrate on which AI-specific change succeeds.

what_transfers: structured experimentation, scaling decisions, and transformation pathways
what_does_not_transfer: the AI framework's explicit responsible-AI controls and data readiness focus
mappings.rationale: Innovation maturity often predicts how well institutions operationalise AI initiatives.

what_transfers: capability development, support models, and sustained skill growth
what_does_not_transfer: AI-specific literacy and specialist capability content
mappings.rationale: This is the clearest sibling mapping between the two Jisc models.

what_transfers: quality of knowledge assets, access, and evidence use
what_does_not_transfer: the AI model's stronger emphasis on governance for machine-use data flows
mappings.rationale: Good knowledge management often signals better readiness for responsible AI.

mappings.target_construct: AI Strategy & Leadership / Ethics & Responsible AI
what_transfers: external partnership and sector learning that influence AI choices
what_does_not_transfer: the absence of a dedicated partnership dimension in the AI model
mappings.rationale: Knowledge exchange shapes AI maturity indirectly rather than through a one-to-one structural match.

what_does_not_transfer: THE DMI does not isolate partnership maturity as a dedicated top-level construct
mappings.rationale: This gap should be preserved as a non-mapping rather than forced into a single THE child dimension.
